[
{"text":"Polio, smallpox, and many other devastating diseases were brought under control largely thanks to vaccines developed through animal experiments.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Animals experience pain and fear much as humans do, so inflicting suffering on them for human gain is a grave moral wrong.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Humans hold a higher moral status than other species, so human lives rightly take priority over animal welfare.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Every animal is the subject of its own life and holds a right not to be used as a research tool.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Regulated animal testing is the safest way to screen new drugs before they are given to human volunteers.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Results from rodents often fail to predict how drugs behave in humans, which makes animal experiments an unreliable basis for medicine.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Modern oversight committees and welfare laws keep suffering in laboratories to a minimum and make animal research ethically acceptable.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Laboratory animals endure confinement, injury, and death, and no welfare regulation can make that treatment humane.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Computer models and cell cultures cannot yet reproduce a whole living body, so living animals remain necessary for studying complex diseases.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Organ-on-a-chip technology, human tissue cultures, and computer simulation can already replace most animal experiments.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Banning animal research would condemn countless patients to preventable death while sparing animals only a small share of the suffering humans cause.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Society has no right to treat sentient creatures as disposable instruments, just as it has no right to experiment on unwilling humans.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Most major Nobel Prize winning advances in physiology and medicine relied on experiments with animals.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Many drugs that passed animal trials went on to harm or kill people, which proves animal data cannot guarantee human safety.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Animals have no moral duties or rational autonomy, so they cannot hold rights that override the needs of sick humans.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Judging a being's worth by its intelligence or species is a prejudice comparable to racism and sexism.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Religious traditions give humans stewardship over animals, and using them to heal the sick falls within that mandate.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Compassion toward all living creatures is a core religious duty that forbids deliberately causing animals to suffer for profit or curiosity.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Surgeons gain life-saving techniques by practicing and testing procedures on animals before operating on human patients.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Funding spent on animal laboratories would produce better health outcomes if redirected to human-based research and prevention.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Because animal experiments are legally required before human trials, abolishing them would leave drug safety unprotected.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Pharmaceutical companies rely on animal testing mainly to shield themselves from liability, not because it benefits patients.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Animals used in research are bred for that purpose, so their use does not take anything from wild populations or nature.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Millions of animals die in laboratories every year, a mass killing that no medical benefit could excuse.","side":"B"},
{"text":"A researcher who refuses animal experiments when they could cure a disease bears responsibility for the human deaths that follow.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Past abuses in laboratories show that researchers cannot be trusted to police their own treatment of animals.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Genetically engineered mice allow scientists to study cancer and inherited diseases in ways that no other method can match.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Humans differ so much from mice, monkeys, and dogs in biology that findings from those species mislead researchers more than they help.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Reducing, refining, and replacing animals gradually is a sensible path, but total abolition would stall medical progress.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Any medical progress built on torturing the defenseless is morally tainted and should be abandoned.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Veterinary medicine also benefits from animal research, so animals themselves gain from the treatments tested on them.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Animals cannot consent to experiments, so using them is exploitation no matter what humans gain.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Public health depends on animal testing to detect toxic chemicals before they reach consumers, workers, and children.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Cosmetics and household products are tested on animals to little purpose, and this shows research on animals is often trivial and wasteful.","side":"B"},
{"text":"The suffering of a mouse in a lab is a small price compared with the lives saved by the cure it helps produce.","side":"A"},
{"text":"No quantity of human benefit can balance the agony of a monkey locked in a cage and subjected to repeated procedures.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Countries that ban animal experiments would simply import medical advances developed elsewhere, free-riding on the animal research of others.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Phasing out animal research would push scientists to build better human-relevant methods and make medicine more accurate.","side":"B"},
{"text":"Vaccines against COVID-19 reached the public rapidly only because animal studies confirmed their safety and effectiveness first.","side":"A"},
{"text":"Every species that feels pain deserves legal protection from experiments, and laws allowing laboratory use are as unjust as slavery once was.","side":"B"}
]
